subject: Social Science
central_question: How do major physical features of the world shape climate, ecosystems, resources, trade and human life, and why must people understand and protect them?
in_scope_units: The complexity of mapping the Earth and the limits of map projections
The oceans: water, currents, trenches, coral reefs and smaller water bodies and waterways
Asia: the Tibetan Plateau, Gobi Desert, Eurasian Steppes and Ural Mountains
Europe: the European Plain and major mountain landscapes
Africa: the Sahara, savannah and River Nile
South America: the Andes, Amazon basin and Atacama Desert
North America: the Colorado Plateau, Rocky Mountains and related physical features
Australia and Antarctica: deserts, distinctive ecosystems and human adaptation
Environmental pressures, interdependence and sustainable management of major landscapes
banned_topics: Detailed Indian physical geography covered in the preceding part of the textbook
Political boundaries or country histories unrelated to the chapter’s physical-geography tour
Detailed plate-tectonics theory beyond the chapter’s use of tectonic movement to explain selected landforms

known_pitfalls.claim: A flat world map can reproduce the Earth perfectly without distortion.
known_pitfalls.correction: The Earth is an oblate spheroid, so every flat map projection involves some compromise in size, shape or other spatial relationships.

known_pitfalls.claim: The ocean floor is a flat plain.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter states that the ocean floor, like land, contains mountains, valleys, plains and very deep trenches.
The chapter includes both hot deserts and cold deserts and identifies Antarctica as the largest desert on Earth.

known_pitfalls.claim: Coral reefs are threatened only by natural causes.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter links threats to reefs with human activities such as overfishing, pollution and climate change, and discusses coral bleaching.

recommended_example_progression: Questions and activities 1: explain why all map projections contain some distortion
Questions and activities 4: explain how oceans regulate the Earth’s climate
Questions and activities 2: explain what makes the Tibetan Plateau unique
Questions and activities 6: analyse why the Amazon Rainforest is often called the “Lungs of the Earth”
Questions and activities 9: trace causes, impacts and possible solutions for deforestation, reef bleaching or desertification
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with the section “Questions and activities”, containing questions and applied tasks 1-11.
